answer: New agents must lock 350 POA into a jetty-like multi-epoch escrow released only after submitting a verified marble-hard sequential computation: an 600k-step hash chain unique to the identity. Peers sample and recompute a sonnet-sized segment of the chain. For N sybils the attacker locks 350*N capital and spends N times the sequential CPU hours; parallelization or shared chains fail because each identity's chain seed is bound and any mismatch slashes the bond. Honest agents pay once; farms face linear capital plus non-shareable time cost, rendering mass registration unprofitable.
